purpose: Record the terminal KEEP decision for polling and socket2 after a source-pinned cross-platform surface inventory and canonical marginal-ledger review. This packet performs no replacement implementation and authorizes no source, manifest, lockfile, or dependency change.

authority.decision_basis: The plan already classifies both dependencies KEEP. Their direct native edges cover reactor registration, wake, readiness modes, descriptor or handle lifecycle, socket creation, addresses, keepalive, and platform-specific options. The canonical ledger records only a small marginal graph benefit, no marginal native code, build script, or proc macro, and no evidence of a rustix eviction. No named incumbent defect, applicable advisory, owner-chartered suite-wide platform project, or meaningful marginal-cost change was found.

polling_semantic_matrix.current_semantics: create_reactor chooses epoll or optional io_uring on Linux/Android, kqueue on Apple/BSD, IOCP-backed polling on Windows, BrowserReactor on wasm, and Unsupported elsewhere.
All native adapters reject duplicate tokens and duplicate raw descriptors or sockets before delegating registration to polling.
Adapters preserve bookkeeping on hard delete failures, remove already-gone registrations, and expose NotFound for unknown tokens. Epoll additionally tracks orphan tombstones.
The resolved polling implementation retries Interrupted waits against a fixed deadline; repository adapters call Poller::wait directly while the Reactor trait still permits Interrupted errors.
Normal IoDriver registrations use generation-tagged TokenSlab entries and retire a slot instead of wrapping its maximum generation. Raw Reactor callers may provide arbitrary tokens.

Epoll compares an fstat dev/inode/mode tuple before and after add and during lifecycle operations. Kqueue checks only descriptor validity. Windows tracks raw socket values without a generation identity.
All native adapters delegate wake to Poller::notify; IoDriver serializes a single active poll leader. Some pre-registration and rearm wake errors are intentionally ignored.

Epoll and kqueue map default registrations to Oneshot, edge to Edge, and edge plus oneshot to EdgeOneshot. Windows rejects public mode flags while polling's default add remains oneshot. No public route selects PollMode::Level.
Epoll masks read and write by registered interest, preserves error and HUP sidebands, and filters priority. Kqueue derives a narrower read/write/HUP view. Windows maps only read and write.
IoRegistration and Registration provide RAII cleanup and one retry, while generational tokens reject stale driver events. Persistent backend delete errors can still outlive local driver state.
The exported Registration catches deregistration panics and retries cleanup, but its constructor is test-only and no production backend wiring through ReactorHandle was found.
No reactor or driver atfork hook, process-identity ownership check, child reinitialization path, or inherited-poller policy was found.

socket_semantic_matrix.current_semantics: socket2 creates IPv4/IPv6 TCP sockets and Unix stream sockets, applies nonblocking mode, and converts successful sockets into std ownership.
SockAddr bridges IP socket addresses and Unix path addresses for bind and connect paths.

Linux abstract Unix connect encodes a leading NUL into SockAddr::unix, and source contains a std-listener interoperability path. Empty, maximum-length, and embedded-NUL boundary cases are not retained in this packet.
Borrowed SockRef configures TCP keepalive, observes or tunes UDP buffers, and applies best-effort ATP control-stream buffer hints without transferring socket ownership.
TcpKeepalive carries idle, interval, and retry parameters; unsupported interval or retry platforms return Unsupported instead of silently ignoring requests.
TCP creation paths cover reuse-address, conditionally available reuse-port, IPv6-only, nodelay, bind, listen backlog, and nonblocking conversion.
UDP creation remains in std; SockRef observes and tunes bounded receive and send buffer sizes. Observation failures become absent values while setter failures propagate.
Nonblocking TCP and Unix connect classify in-progress and Interrupted states, wait for readiness, inspect socket error or peer state, and stop fallback when cancellation is observed.
Owned socket2 values close on early return; successful paths transfer ownership to std sockets. Registration ownership and cancellation checkpoints remain coupled to connect and I/O paths.

planned_evidence.interpretation: Planned evidence identifies the size of a future parity project. It is not needed to retain incumbents and does not authorize replacement, cutover, or a cross-platform correctness claim.

gaps.detail: The registry omits four current production direct socket2 owner paths.
The canonical ledger predates the claim revision and was only corroborated by current static declaration and lock-version checks.
The marginal ledger has macOS, Windows, Linux, and wasm targets but no BSD target.
Fork-after-reactor initialization safety and child reinitialization are unproven and undocumented in source.
Descriptor validity checks cannot distinguish close-and-reuse between checks and operations.
Raw socket value tracking has no handle-generation identity.
No public route selects PollMode::Level; existing level wording does not prove repeated level delivery.
Some wake errors are intentionally ignored and no recovery receipt is retained here.
The exported Registration documents a production path, but construction is test-only and production ReactorHandle wiring was not found.
No retained live macOS, BSD, Windows, or Android receipt proves the complete declared reactor and socket-option surface.
No retained macOS, BSD, or Windows applied-value receipt covers keepalive interval and retry behavior.
Abstract Unix empty, maximum-length, and embedded-NUL name cases are not covered by this static packet.
The connected-error conformance case permits ambiguous network filtering and is not strong per-platform evidence.
One TcpSocket reuse-port surface is cfg(unix), broader than upstream availability on every Unix-like target.

It does not prove live Linux, Android, macOS, BSD, Windows, wasm, or other-platform behavior.

It does not prove applied keepalive or socket-option values on macOS, BSD, or Windows.
The historical canonical marginal ledger is graph evidence only; it does not prove current compilation, runtime behavior, performance, release readiness, or broad workspace health.
Marginal native status none does not certify the full root graph as native-code-free; root native status remains unknown in most recorded rows.
KEEP does not bless the routed incumbent-hardening gaps and does not convert planned evidence into executed evidence.
